ideas.from: syed3000 loaders inside dfthcsos 91d0ad25 (see the dfthcsos table above); studied 2026-11-12 by the QCC-49 agent after our paper-first loader stalled at the unary-iteration cost
ideas.generator: Not yet implemented. `src/dfthcsos_gen` has only the unary-iteration loader (Babbush et al. 2018). What we learned and will rewrite fresh: about 75 temporary ANDs (all products of the high address bits) feed about 200 CCX whose controls are address bits XORed in place with those products (by CX) and whose targets are word bits, so each output bit is a short sum of products of two linear forms; the table has to be fitted to that family.
ideas.technique: Angle loader as a rank-1 quadratic form per output bit: structure of the public dfthcsos `angle_k` circuits seen as an aggregate (gate-type counts, which register each CCX controls and targets), not copied

ideas.from: Khattar et al. 2025 (paper); public notebook text for the qubit total
ideas.generator: `src/dqi_gen/decoder.py`, `src/dqi_gen/tower.py` (our own rows-only formulation and tower division)
ideas.technique: DQI: nothing learned from any public circuit file (ADR-0009 rule 3). Our generator uses the paper's divstep idea (Khattar et al., arXiv:2510.10967 section II B 3, Bernstein-Yang divsteps) and our own tower-field derivation; the only public-derived fact is the reported 892-qubit total (notebook text), which tells us the frontier keeps its state in or beside the 840 syndrome qubits.

ideas.from: alexchilton notebook text on jday96314's decoder (section 3); Khattar & Gidney (2024)
ideas.generator: `src/dqi_gen/jacobi.py` (classical reference); circuit generator `src/dqi_gen/lanczos.py` if it lands
ideas.technique: DQI: the 892-qubit decoder is a continued-fraction (Schur-type) design whose pair of polynomials is updated by `(N, B) <- (l N + q B, N)`, with an amplitude polynomial so the scan costs about 11 Toffolis per point (notebook text only, no circuit or generator read). We derived our own Jacobi/Lanczos solver and Gauss-quadrature Forney from standard numerical analysis (Chebyshev algorithm, orthogonal polynomials over GF(2^12)); the amplitude-polynomial idea is not implemented.

DQI: a GF(2^12) multiplier of bilinear rank 42 exists (number only, from the public notebook text via our own notes; no circuit or generator read). We derived our own rank-42 algorithm (degree-4 extension of GF(8), 7 evaluation points, 6 ANDs per GF(8) product) and tower inversion from standard algebra.

ideas.from: Gu et al., arXiv 2610.22367 (paper main text)
ideas.generator: Not implemented; candidate for `src/dqi_gen` under ADR-0009 stage 1
ideas.technique: Berlekamp-Massey with a rescaled update (no polynomial history) and a one-entry history stack priced as a rare failure (about 1e-4 of inputs)

ideas.from: Gu, Kemeny, Yelin, Lukin, arXiv:2610.22367 SI I.1; https://github.com/andigu/uncompute `tasks/dqi-reed-solomon` README (Apache-2.0 stated)
ideas.generator: Ranked in `docs/research/dqi.md`; implemented in `src/dqi_gen/` where noted in `docs/experiments/dqi-stage2.md`
ideas.technique: DQI (stage 2, amendment of 2026-11-13): phase-only recovery (the DQI phase is one bit, `Tr(mu_j e_j)`, so Forney needs only a bilinear form of `omega(beta)` and a reciprocal polynomial `Psi` with `Psi sigma' = 1 mod sigma`, 23 Toffolis per scan position); `Psi` by a half-degree Euclid on the even and odd parts of `sigma` (characteristic 2); dialog-free Berlekamp-Massey by the invariant `sigma_0 delta = 1` and a one-entry history stack; adaptive coefficient ranges from the DQI weight law. Read in the paper text and the task README only; no circuit file. The public DQI lineage has no licence; this source states Apache-2.0.
